sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Israel has been fighting Hamas in Gaza for almost a year.
sentences.zh: 以色列与哈马斯在加沙的战斗已经持续了近一年。

sentences.en: But despite catastrophic losses, Hamas seems no closer to declaring defeat.
sentences.zh: 但尽管损失惨重，哈马斯似乎离宣布战败还很远。

sentences.en: And despite considerable military gains, Israel seems no closer to declaring victory.
sentences.zh: 尽管在军事上取得了相当大的进展，以色列似乎也离宣布胜利还很远。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Patrick Kingsley on why the war in Gaza is still going and what it would take to end it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事帕特里克·金斯利将探讨为何加沙战争仍在继续，以及结束战争需要什么条件。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月28日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Patrick, we wanted to hear from you in Israel today because we're coming up nearly on a year since October 7th.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克，我们今天想听听你在以色列的见解，因为距离10月7日已经快一年了。

sentences.en: It really feels like every week you write at least one story about the ceasefire negotiations.
sentences.zh: 感觉你每周至少要写一篇关于停火谈判的报道。

sentences.en: Some weeks, it looks like progress toward a ceasefire deal.
sentences.zh: 有些周看起来像是朝着停火协议迈进。

sentences.en: Other weeks, no progress.
sentences.zh: 而有些周则毫无进展。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the threat of a wider war in the Middle East is deepening.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，中东爆发更大规模战争的威胁正在加深。

sentences.en: Just this weekend, there was a huge exchange of rocket fire in Israel's northern border with
sentences.zh: 就在这个周末，以色列北部边境与

sentences.en: Lebanon.
sentences.zh: 黎巴嫩之间发生了大规模的火箭弹交火。

sentences.en: You know, that doesn't seem likely to end while the war in Gaza is still going.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只要加沙战争还在继续，这种情况似乎就不太可能结束。

sentences.en: So we all felt like it was really time to come to you and ask a basic question, which is, why can't they agree to a ceasefire?
sentences.zh: 所以我们都觉得是时候来问你一个基本问题了：为什么他们无法就停火达成一致？

sentences.en: And perhaps more fundamentally, why is this war in Gaza still going on?
sentences.zh: 更根本的问题是，为什么加沙战争还在持续？

sentences.en: So these are very good questions.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常好的问题。

sentences.en: Both the questions come down to two men, essentially.
sentences.zh: 这两个问题本质上都归结为两个人。

sentences.en: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel and Yahya Sinwar of Hamas.
sentences.zh: 以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡和哈马斯领导人叶海亚·辛瓦尔。

sentences.en: And to understand why they have such fundamentally mutually exclusive positions on the war, we
sentences.zh: 要理解为什么他们在战争问题上持有如此根本性的互斥立场，我们

sentences.en: have to start with the ceasefire, which is the most basic building block for stopping the war.
sentences.zh: 必须从停火开始，这是停止战争最基本的基石。

sentences.en: And the two leaders have a fundamental disagreement here.
sentences.zh: 而这两位领导人在这一点上存在根本分歧。

sentences.en: Netanyahu, the Israeli leader, essentially wants a temporary ceasefire.
sentences.zh: 以色列领导人内塔尼亚胡本质上想要的是临时停火。

sentences.en: Sinwar, the leader of Hamas, wants a permanent ceasefire.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯领导人辛瓦尔想要的是永久停火。

sentences.en: So, Patrick, explain that.
sentences.zh: 那么，帕特里克，解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: Start maybe with Netanyahu.
sentences.zh: 也许先从内塔尼亚胡开始。

sentences.en: Explain that position.
sentences.zh: 解释一下他的立场。

sentences.en: So, for Prime Minister Netanyahu, the professed goal of the war is to destroy Hamas, to destroy
sentences.zh: 对于内塔尼亚胡总理来说，战争的公开目标是摧毁哈马斯，摧毁

sentences.en: this group that invaded Israel on October 7th, killed more than 1,000 people, and abducted roughly 250.
sentences.zh: 这个在10月7日入侵以色列、杀害了1000多人并绑架了约250人的组织。

sentences.en: And key members of his far-right coalition will accept nothing less than Hamas's total defeat.
sentences.zh: 他极右翼联盟中的关键成员绝不接受哈马斯的彻底失败。

sentences.en: And so, if the ceasefire is temporary, it will allow him to present the truce to his base as
sentences.zh: 因此，如果停火是临时的，他就可以向其支持者展示，这只是为了释放

sentences.en: just a brief measure to free some of the roughly 100 hostages still left inside Gaza, after which Israel can easily return to the fighting and to defeating Hamas.
sentences.zh: 目前仍留在加沙的约100名人质中的一部分而采取的短暂措施，之后以色列可以轻松恢复战斗并击败哈马斯。

sentences.en: So, it will allow him to get some of the hostages back, thus placating the many Israelis whose top
sentences.zh: 所以，这能让他救回部分人质，从而安抚那些将人质获释视为首要任务的以色列人，

sentences.en: priority is the release of the hostages, and it will take away some of Hamas's key bargaining chips, and it would allow him to say to his base that, don't worry,
sentences.zh: 同时也能剥夺哈马斯的一些关键谈判筹码，并让他能对支持者说，别担心，

sentences.en: the war will continue and Hamas will be defeated after this brief pause in hostilities.
sentences.zh: 战争将会继续，哈马斯将在这次短暂的敌对行动暂停后被击败。

sentences.en: And what's the calculation for Sinwar?
sentences.zh: 那么辛瓦尔的算盘是什么？

sentences.en: Walk us through his reasons for pushing through a permanent ceasefire.
sentences.zh: 请为我们梳理一下他坚持要求永久停火的原因。

sentences.en: Well, if he goes for a temporary one, he gives up key bargaining chips, the Israeli hostages who Hamas captured on October 7th, and he doesn't get much in return.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果他接受临时停火，他就会放弃关键的谈判筹码——哈马斯在10月7日俘获的以色列人质，而且他得不到多少回报。

sentences.en: He doesn't secure Hamas's survival, and he leaves open the possibility that fighting will resume, that Israel will continue its campaign after a few weeks,
sentences.zh: 他无法确保哈马斯的生存，而且留下了战斗可能恢复的可能性，即以色列在几周后继续其军事行动，

sentences.en: and will continue to erode Hamas's fighting capability and governing capability, and eventually secure its defeat.
sentences.zh: 并继续削弱哈马斯的战斗能力和治理能力，最终确保其失败。

sentences.en: A permanent ceasefire, by contrast, essentially allows Hamas to survive the war intact as a political movement,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，永久停火本质上允许哈马斯作为一场政治运动在战争中幸存下来，

sentences.en: intact as a depleted but still active governing force that controls Gaza.
sentences.zh: 作为一个虽然被削弱但仍然活跃的、控制着加沙的治理力量继续存在。

sentences.en: It may not be enough to save his life, Israel will probably pursue him for the rest of his days, but it allows Hamas as a movement to survive the war.
sentences.zh: 这可能不足以保住他的性命，以色列可能会追捕他余生，但这允许哈马斯作为一个运动在战争中存活。

sentences.en: Okay, so these sides are pretty dug in on their respective very far apart positions, but of course talks have been bumping along, right?
sentences.zh: 好的，双方在各自相去甚远的立场上都相当固执，但谈判当然一直在磕磕绊绊地进行，对吧？

sentences.en: And they are bumping along with the help of the United States and Secretary of State Antony Blinken.
sentences.zh: 而且是在美国和国务卿安东尼·布林肯的帮助下磕磕绊绊地进行。

sentences.en: What, if anything, has the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国在谈判中的参与对这个过程意味着什么（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: involvement in the talks meant for this process?
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 在双方——以色列和哈马斯，以及调解方埃及和卡塔尔——感到缺乏动力、政治意愿

sentences.en: has brought key energy at times when it feels like both the sides, Israel and Hamas, and the mediators, Egypt and Qatar, have lacked energy, political will,
sentences.zh: 或坐到谈判桌前的欲望时，注入了关键的能量。

sentences.en: or desire to sit down at a negotiating table.
sentences.zh: 特别是，他们一直试图弥合各方之间的分歧，

sentences.en: In particular, they've been trying to bridge the gaps between the different sides,
sentences.zh: 他们的主要方法是在双方反复争论的协议草案文本中，采用一种“建设性的模糊性”。

sentences.en: and their main approach has been a kind of constructive ambiguity in the language that is written in the draft agreements that the two sides have been haggling over.
sentences.zh: “建设性的模糊性”到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: What does that mean exactly, constructive ambiguity?
sentences.zh: 这意味着在协议的措辞中保持足够的灵活性，以便双方都能向各自的支持者推销该协议，称其实现了支持者想要的目标。

sentences.en: It means having enough fluidity in the language of the deal so that both sides can sell the agreement to their bases as something that achieves what those bases want.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，不要在协议措辞上过于严苛，而是保持措辞足够宽松，以便双方都能向各自民众推销。

sentences.en: So in other words, not be so forensic in the wording of the agreement, like keeping the language loose enough so that both sides can sell it to their populations.
sentences.zh: 所以这本质上是美国试图在这里带来的政治解决方案。

sentences.en: So this is essentially a political fix the U.S.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: is trying to bring here.
sentences.zh: 举个例子说明这种措辞上的“建设性模糊”是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 在谈判的某个阶段，

sentences.en: And just to give an example of how that constructive ambiguity in the language worked.
sentences.zh: 关于以色列在多大程度上保留沿分隔加沙南北的一条特定通道的军事存在，双方陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: At one point in the negotiation,
sentences.zh: 以色列希望在那里维持检查站，以阻止哈马斯在两个区域之间运送武器。

sentences.en: there was a standoff over the extent to which Israel would retain a military presence along a particular thoroughfare dividing northern Gaza from southern Gaza.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯过去和现在都不希望在那个位置有以色列的检查站。

sentences.en: Israel wanted to maintain checkpoints there to stop Hamas moving weapons between those two areas.
sentences.zh: 所以谈判代表弥合这一分歧的方式，至少在某个阶段，是将这一理念的原则包含在协议草案中，

sentences.en: Hamas didn't and doesn't want Israeli checkpoints in that location.
sentences.zh: 但没有包含实施该计划的具体执行机制。

sentences.en: So the way that the negotiators bridged that gap, at least at one point, was to include the principle of that idea within the draft agreement,
sentences.zh: 这本可以让以色列领导层，即内塔尼亚胡，回到他的右翼支持者面前说，不，

sentences.en: but not the enforcement mechanism by which that plan would be enacted.
sentences.zh: 防止加沙人运送武器的原则已经得到了维护。

sentences.en: And that would have allowed the Israeli leadership, Netanyahu, to go back to his right-wing base and say, no,
sentences.zh: 这也本可以让哈马斯在内部辩称，好吧，是的，原则确实在里面，

sentences.en: the principle of preventing Gazans from moving weapons around Gaza has been maintained.
sentences.zh: 但协议草案中没有任何关于执行机制的提及。

sentences.en: And it would have allowed Hamas to argue internally that, well, yes, that principle is in there,
sentences.zh: 对，那里没有检查站。

sentences.en: but there is nothing mentioned in that draft agreement about an enforcement mechanism.
sentences.zh: 你在说什么检查站？

sentences.en: Right, there's no checkpoints there.
sentences.zh: 我们可以自由移动。

sentences.en: What checkpoints are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: We are free to move.
sentences.zh: 但到了7月，我们看到了这种“建设性模糊”为何行不通。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 虽然双方似乎在5月就这种模糊术语达成了一致，但两个月后的7月，

sentences.en: But then in July, we got a window into how this constructive ambiguity doesn't quite work.
sentences.zh: 以色列提出了新的要求，希望用更清晰的措辞取代这种模糊性。

sentences.en: While the two sides seem to have agreed on this ambiguous terminology in May, by July, two months later,
sentences.zh: 他们想要明确关于阻止加沙人携带武器在领土内移动的原则将如何执行。

sentences.en: Israel had come back with a new demand to replace that ambiguity with greater clarity.
sentences.zh: 当然，这消除了模糊性，而这仍然是哈马斯不愿同意的事情。

sentences.en: They wanted clarity on that principle of stopping Gazans from moving around the territory with guns could be enforced.
sentences.zh: 这是阻碍双方达成协议的众多绊脚石之一。

sentences.en: And, of course, that removed the ambiguity and remains something that Hamas does not want to agree to.
sentences.zh: 好的，从我们所知的一切来看，谈判并没有奏效，或者至少正如你所说，进展非常缓慢。

sentences.en: And it is one of many stumbling blocks that is preventing a deal between the two sides.
sentences.zh: 但让我们谈谈战争通常是如何结束的，即一方承认自己无法再获胜。

sentences.en: OK, so from all we can tell, the talks are not working, or at least they're proving very cumbersome as you're laying out here.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，那似乎应该是哈马斯。

sentences.en: But let's talk about how wars normally end, which is that one side admits it can no longer win.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，截至本月，据加沙卫生官员称，已有4万名加沙人死亡，其大片领土已成废墟。

sentences.en: And in this case, that would appear to be Hamas.
sentences.zh: 那么为什么这一切加起来，哈马斯却不认为这是一场失败呢？

sentences.en: I mean, as of this month, 40,000 Gazans were dead, according to Gazan health officials, and vast swaths of its territory are in ruins.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个非常合理的问题，因为当你看着加沙，看到所有令人震惊的破坏时，

sentences.en: So why doesn't all of that add up to Hamas viewing this as a defeat?
sentences.zh: 超过一半的房屋受损，数万人丧生，基础设施和卫生系统遭受巨大破坏。

sentences.en: Well, that's a very reasonable question, because when you look at Gaza and you see all the astonishing destruction,
sentences.zh: 你确实会想，为什么哈马斯不投降？在大多数其他战争中，损失达到这种程度的一方，此时早已投降了。

sentences.en: more than half the houses damaged, tens of thousands of people killed, huge harm to infrastructure and to the health system.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一场正常的战争。

sentences.en: You do wonder, why doesn't Hamas surrender in most other wars, a side that is lost materially to this extent, would have surrendered by this point.
sentences.zh: 双方对胜利的门槛非常不寻常。

sentences.en: But this is not a normal war.
sentences.zh: 以色列对胜利的门槛非常高。

sentences.en: The sides have very unusual thresholds for victory.
sentences.zh: 其领导人内塔尼亚胡表示，他想要彻底摧毁哈马斯。

sentences.en: Israel has a very high threshold for victory.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯对胜利的门槛非常低。

sentences.en: Its leader, Netanyahu, says he wants the total destruction of Hamas.
sentences.zh: 它只想生存下去。

sentences.en: Hamas has a very low threshold for victory.
sentences.zh: 这两个门槛都不太典型。

sentences.en: It just wants to survive.
sentences.zh: 通常当一方如此令人信服地摧毁另一方时，想想1945年的日本，日本人投降了。

sentences.en: And neither threshold is very typical.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你看看第二次世界大战中法国意识到自己即将战败的其他时刻，

sentences.en: Usually when one side so convincingly destroys another, think of Japan in 1945, the Japanese surrendered.
sentences.zh: 其领导人并没有等待法国被彻底摧毁才逃跑或屈服。

sentences.en: Alternatively, if you look at other moments in the Second World War when France realized it was losing,
sentences.zh: 我们这里的情况是，一方按常规衡量标准正在战败，但不想投降，因为其自身的胜利门槛太低，

sentences.en: its leaders did not wait for the total destruction of France to either flee or give in.
sentences.zh: 以至于它甚至认为自己可能实际上正在获胜。

sentences.en: And what we have here is we have a side that by conventional measures is losing, but doesn't want to surrender because its own threshold for victory is so low
sentences.zh: 所以对哈马斯来说，只要还有一个战士站着，本质上，它就还在战争中，并没有输掉战争。

sentences.en: that it kind of thinks that it might actually be winning.
sentences.zh: 它还在继续。

sentences.en: So for Hamas, as long as it has one fighter standing, essentially, it's still in the war and hasn't lost the war.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It's still going.
sentences.zh: 而且让这一切变得加倍反常规的是，以色列军队本身并没有以一种特别正常的方式进行战斗。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 它并没有占领它所征服的领土。

sentences.en: And what makes all this doubly unconventional is the fact that the Israeli army is itself not fighting in a particularly normal way.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们并没有控制加沙，尽管事实上在过去10个月的某个时刻，他们已经占领了大部分地区。

sentences.en: It is not holding the territory that it conquers.
sentences.zh: 由于他们没有建立控制权，这就导致了一种非常离奇的“打地鼠”游戏：以色列进入一个地区，与哈马斯进行了一场极具破坏性的战斗，

sentences.en: And what that means is they are not controlling Gaza, despite the fact that they have captured most of it by now at some point during the last 10 months.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯离开，哈马斯返回，迫使以色列再次回来，进行第二次，有时是第三次和第四次战斗，然后仍然放弃控制权，

sentences.en: And because they haven't established control, that leads to this very bizarre form of whack-a-mole where Israel goes into an area, has a very destructive battle with Hamas,
sentences.zh: 再次撤退到加沙内部甚至以色列境内的关键战略位置。

sentences.en: Hamas leaves, Hamas returns, forcing Israel to come back, fighting a second, sometimes a third and a fourth time, and still then abandoning its control,
sentences.zh: 整个循环又重新开始。

sentences.en: retreating again to key strategic positions within Gaza or even within Israel.
sentences.zh: 所以这导致了巨大的破坏，但并没有特别导致加沙地面实际控制权的变化。

sentences.en: And the whole cycle begins again.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克，为什么他们不占领他们已经拿下的地区？

sentences.en: So it leads to extraordinary destruction, but it doesn't particularly lead to a change in who actually controls Gaza on the ground.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们应该在这里说明，对于许多巴勒斯坦人来说，

sentences.en: And Patrick, why don't they occupy the areas that they've taken?
sentences.zh: 以色列从未停止占领加沙。

sentences.en: Well, we should say here that for a lot of Palestinians,
sentences.zh: 他们在1967年至2005年间在加沙内部保持了实际存在，直到以色列士兵和定居者离开该领土。

sentences.en: Israel never stopped occupying Gaza.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，他们仍然对贸易、领空、电话网络、出入境保持着某种程度的控制。

sentences.en: They maintained a physical presence inside Gaza between 1967 and 2005, when Israeli soldiers and Israeli settlers left the territory.
sentences.zh: 以色列人之间的争论是他们是否应该像2005年之前那样回到保持实际存在的状态。

sentences.en: But ever since, they've still maintained some degree of control over trade, the airspace, the phone networks, entry and exit.
sentences.zh: 目前，那些反对这种实际存在的人似乎已经占了上风。

sentences.en: The debate among Israelis is whether they should go back to maintaining a physical presence as they did until 2005.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: And for the moment, those opposed to that physical presence seem to have worn out.
sentences.zh: 因为在整个加沙部署士兵真的很难。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 这需要大量的资源。

sentences.en: Because installing soldiers throughout Gaza is really difficult.
sentences.zh: 这很复杂，而且也很危险。

sentences.en: It requires vast amounts of resources.
sentences.zh: 它必须由数千名以色列士兵保护。

sentences.en: It's complicated, and it's also dangerous.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图守住加沙这样大小的领土，他们随时可能被杀。

sentences.en: It has to be protected by thousands of Israeli soldiers.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，以色列领导层似乎不想考虑这种可能性，

sentences.en: They can be killed at any time if you try and hang on to a territory the size of Gaza.
sentences.zh: 至少目前是这样，即使政府内部和以色列右翼公众中有大量人

sentences.en: And because of that, it seems like Israel's leadership does not want to entertain that possibility,
sentences.zh: 实际上希望看到以色列回到在加沙地带建立军事基地的状态。

sentences.en: at least for now, even if there are people within government and in vast ways of the Israeli right-wing public
sentences.zh: 所以如果地面局势无法结束战争，而停火似乎也不太可能，至少目前如此，那么战争如何结束？

sentences.en: that would actually like to see Israel return to building military bases across the Gaza Strip.
sentences.zh: 这正开始成为关键问题。

sentences.en: So if the situation on the ground won't end the war, and a ceasefire seems improbable, at least for now, then how does the war end?
sentences.zh: 这两方如何走出这场战争？

sentences.en: That is starting to become the key question.
sentences.zh: 他们如何找到一条出路，摆脱这种似乎已经变得棘手的局面？

sentences.en: How do these two sides get out of this war?
sentences.zh: 而且感觉我们似乎需要某种改变游戏规则的东西，也许是我们迄今为止还没有完全构想出来的东西，

sentences.en: How do they find a way through what feels like it has become an intractable situation?
sentences.zh: 一个“黑天鹅”事件，将改变这场冲突战斗方式的构造板块。

sentences.en: And it's beginning to feel like we're going to need some kind of game changer, something maybe we haven't quite conceived of so far,
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: a black swan event that is going to shift the tectonic plates of how this conflict is being fought.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜（Wena Liu）。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏《Connections》，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: （注：此条目为空，根据要求保留）

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: （注：此条目为空，根据要求保留）

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《拼字蜜蜂》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的那些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: So, Patrick, we're at this current impasse, in large part because of these two leaders and their political calculations.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克，我们目前陷入僵局，很大程度上是因为这两位领导人及其政治算计。

sentences.en: And it feels like maybe only something really big could change things, as you're saying.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，感觉似乎只有真正重大的事情才能改变现状。

sentences.en: What sort of game changer are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 我们所说的改变游戏规则的因素是指哪种？

sentences.en: Well, there's a few different things that could shift the needle.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几种不同的因素可能会打破僵局。

sentences.en: One could be in the US, one could be with the Israelis, and one could be a regional war that would change the dynamic across the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 一种可能发生在美国，一种可能与以色列人有关，还有一种可能是地区战争，这将改变整个中东的动态。

sentences.en: So maybe start with the United States, which is obviously coming up on a big election.
sentences.zh: 那么也许先从美国开始，显然美国即将迎来一场大选。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And whoever wins that election, we will be left at the end of it with a different president.
sentences.zh: 无论谁赢得那场选举，我们最终都会迎来一位不同的总统。

sentences.en: And that different president could have a slightly different focus and attitude to, if not Israel itself, then the way that Israel is prosecuting this war.
sentences.zh: 而这位不同的总统可能会有略微不同的侧重点和态度，即使不是针对以色列本身，也是针对以色列进行这场战争的方式。

sentences.en: And that might in turn change Benjamin Netanyahu's calculations at the negotiation table.
sentences.zh: 这反过来可能会改变本雅明·内塔尼亚胡在谈判桌上的算计。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有别的吗？

sentences.en: Another wild card would be the killing of Yahya Sinwar, the leader of Hamas.
sentences.zh: 另一个不可控因素是哈马斯领导人叶海亚·辛瓦尔的死亡。

sentences.en: That is perhaps Israel's top goal in Gaza right now.
sentences.zh: 这或许是以色列目前在加沙的首要目标。

sentences.en: They've killed several other key leaders of Hamas.
sentences.zh: 他们已经杀死了哈马斯的其他几位关键领导人。

sentences.en: Yahya Sinwar is the last man standing, essentially.
sentences.zh: 叶海亚·辛瓦尔基本上是最后一人了。

sentences.en: If he goes, if the leader of Hamas goes, that would allow Benjamin Netanyahu to say to his base, mission accomplished.
sentences.zh: 如果他倒下，如果哈马斯领导人倒下，那将使本雅明·内塔尼亚胡能够对他的支持者说，任务完成了。

sentences.en: And that in turn might allow him to agree to a ceasefire on the terms that he previously hadn't agreed to.
sentences.zh: 而这反过来可能会让他同意之前未曾同意的停火条件。

sentences.en: In other words, the far right leaders in his coalition perhaps would be satisfied if Sinwar was killed.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果辛瓦尔被杀，他联盟中的极右翼领导人或许会感到满意。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And on the other side of the border, it's possible that with Sinwar dead, with the most powerful leader within Hamas dead, his subordinates would be more likely to compromise,
sentences.zh: 而在边境的另一边，辛瓦尔死后，随着哈马斯内部最有权势的领导人死亡，他的下属更有可能妥协，

sentences.en: to surrender in his absence.
sentences.zh: 在他缺席的情况下投降。

sentences.en: Of course, that's a big if, and it's very possible that Sinwar's death would not actually change their thinking on a ceasefire or on the war itself all that much.
sentences.zh: 当然，这只是一个很大的假设，辛瓦尔的死很有可能实际上并不会改变他们对停火或战争本身的看法。

sentences.en: But the possibility remains.
sentences.zh: 但这种可能性依然存在。

sentences.en: And Patrick, what about the pressure on Netanyahu and the Israeli government on the part of the hostage families?
sentences.zh: 帕特里克，人质家属对内塔尼亚胡和以色列政府施加的压力又如何呢？

sentences.en: Just on Tuesday, one hostage was actually freed.
sentences.zh: 就在周二，一名人质实际上获释了。

sentences.en: So does this pressure, you know, the protests, everything we've been seeing, amount to some sort of game-changing dynamic for Netanyahu?
sentences.zh: 那么这种压力，你知道，抗议活动，我们所看到的一切，对内塔尼亚胡来说算得上是一种改变游戏规则的动态吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's game-changing.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是改变游戏规则的因素。

sentences.en: For a start, it's been going on for a while, and it obviously hasn't shifted his calculations thus far.
sentences.zh: 首先，这种情况已经持续了一段时间，显然到目前为止并没有改变他的算计。

sentences.en: And secondly, it's interesting you mentioned this hostage rescue on Tuesday, because for some, that actually supports Netanyahu's argument that it's only through more military
sentences.zh: 其次，你提到周二的人质营救很有意思，因为对一些人来说，这实际上支持了内塔尼亚胡的论点，即只有通过更多的军事

sentences.en: action that you can free the hostages.
sentences.zh: 行动才能解救人质。

sentences.en: Not a truce, but further action on the ground by the Israeli military in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 不是休战，而是以色列军队在加沙地面的进一步行动。

sentences.en: And while it's true that there are lots of protesters calling for Netanyahu, for the Israeli government
sentences.zh: 虽然确实有很多抗议者呼吁内塔尼亚胡和以色列政府

sentences.en: to prioritize the hostages' well-being and to cut a deal basically at any price in order
sentences.zh: 优先考虑人质的福祉，并基本上不惜一切代价达成协议，以便

sentences.en: to get the hostages home, the people who are pushing most loudly for that deal are not Netanyahu's own supporters.
sentences.zh: 让人质回家，但最强烈推动达成该协议的人并不是内塔尼亚胡自己的支持者。

sentences.en: His base, their priority is Hamas's defeat.
sentences.zh: 他的支持者，他们的首要任务是击败哈马斯。

sentences.en: And while they may care about the hostages and want them home at some point, their immediate release is not their first priority.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们可能关心人质并希望他们回家，但立即释放他们并不是他们的首要任务。

sentences.en: And Patrick, you mentioned regional war as something that could potentially really shift the dynamic here.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克，你提到地区战争是可能真正改变这里动态的因素。

sentences.en: Talk to me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我谈谈这个。

sentences.en: Well, alongside the Gaza war, we also have smaller simmering conflicts between Israel and
sentences.zh: 嗯，除了加沙战争，以色列与

sentences.en: Hamas's allies across the region.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯在整个地区的盟友之间也存在较小的酝酿中的冲突。

sentences.en: Those are Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen, and the benefactor of all those three groups, Iran.
sentences.zh: 这些盟友包括黎巴嫩的真主党、也门的胡塞武装，以及这三个组织背后的资助者——伊朗。

sentences.en: And to varying degrees, those proxies of Iran and Iran itself have been fighting this low-level conflict against Israel in parallel with the Gaza war since October.
sentences.zh: 在不同程度上，这些伊朗的代理人以及伊朗本身自十月以来一直在与加沙战争并行，对以色列进行这种低强度的冲突。

sentences.en: Now, at any moment, all these smaller conflicts could erupt into much bigger ones.
sentences.zh: 现在，在任何时刻，所有这些较小的冲突都可能演变成更大的冲突。

sentences.en: If either side, if Israel makes a mistake or a miscalculation, if Hezbollah makes a mistake
sentences.zh: 如果任何一方，如果以色列犯错或误判，如果真主党犯错

sentences.en: or a miscalculation, Iran the same, suddenly these conflicts could erupt into an all-out regional war involving all these actors firing on full cylinders.
sentences.zh: 或误判，伊朗也是如此，突然之间这些冲突可能会演变成一场全面爆发的地区战争，所有这些参与者都全力开火。

sentences.en: So far, no side has appeared truly willing to do that.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，没有任何一方表现出真正愿意这样做。

sentences.en: They've always stepped back from the brink.
sentences.zh: 他们总是从边缘退缩。

sentences.en: And on Sunday, we saw Hezbollah and Israel doing exactly that.
sentences.zh: 周日，我们看到真主党和以色列正是这样做的。

sentences.en: But if it does escalate into an all-out regional war, then that would at the very least
sentences.zh: 但如果它确实升级为一场全面的地区战争，那么至少会

sentences.en: consume Israel's energies, draw down its resources, its munition supplies, and possibly make Israel
sentences.zh: 消耗以色列的精力，减少其资源和弹药供应，并可能使以色列

sentences.en: much likelier to agree to a truce in Gaza in order to get all of these conflicts to wind down.
sentences.zh: 更有可能同意在加沙停火，以平息所有这些冲突。

sentences.en: And how would a regional war change the calculations for Sinoir?
sentences.zh: 地区战争将如何改变辛瓦尔的算计？

sentences.en: The feeling is that Sinoir would benefit from a regional war.
sentences.zh: 人们的感觉是，辛瓦尔会从地区战争中受益。

sentences.en: A regional war would distract Israel and potentially even endanger the existence of the Israeli state, depending on how long and how intense that war got.
sentences.zh: 地区战争会分散以色列的注意力，甚至可能危及以色列国家的存在，具体取决于战争持续的时间和强度。

sentences.en: All of this benefits Hamas and all of it benefits Sinoir because the weaker the Israeli state is,
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都对哈马斯有利，对辛瓦尔也有利，因为以色列国家越弱，

sentences.en: the more likely it is to compromise in ceasefire negotiations with Hamas and agree to something that Sinoir thinks is more favorable to Hamas's long-term survival.
sentences.zh: 它在与哈马斯的停火谈判中妥协的可能性就越大，并同意辛瓦尔认为对哈马斯长期生存更有利的条件。

sentences.en: And presumably, on the most extreme scenario, the destruction of Israel is something that he's actually rowing toward, and a big regional war would raise the specter of that.
sentences.zh: 据推测，在最极端的情况下，摧毁以色列是他实际上正在努力实现的目标，而一场大规模的地区战争将引发这种恐惧。

sentences.en: It would certainly increase its chances a notch or two.
sentences.zh: 这肯定会增加一两个百分点的可能性。

sentences.en: Israel is a very strong state.
sentences.zh: 以色列是一个非常强大的国家。

sentences.en: It has perhaps the strongest military in the Middle East, and it would take a lot to dislodge its presence in the region.
sentences.zh: 它拥有中东地区最强大的军队，要动摇其在该地区的存在需要付出巨大努力。

sentences.en: But Hamas has never rescinded the call it made in its founding charter to destroy Israel.
sentences.zh: 但哈马斯从未撤回其在成立宪章中提出的摧毁以色列的呼吁。

sentences.en: And anything that makes Israel less safe would be construed by Hamas as a step toward that goal.
sentences.zh: 任何使以色列变得不安全的事情都会被哈马斯解读为朝着该目标迈出的一步。

sentences.en: Now, interestingly, there are those who believe that the Israelis themselves, or some Israelis, are also seeking a regional war.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，有些人认为以色列人自己，或者一些以色列人，也在寻求一场地区战争。

sentences.en: Well, by this theory, it would create the pretext by which Israel could attack Iran in a much more brazen and intense way than it ever previously has done.
sentences.zh: 嗯，根据这个理论，这将创造一个借口，使以色列能够以比以往任何时候都更厚颜无耻和更激烈的方式攻击伊朗。

sentences.en: Prime Minister Netanyahu and many Israelis see Iran as their biggest foe, and they fear that the nuclear weapons program that Iran is working on
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡总理和许多以色列人将伊朗视为他们最大的敌人，他们担心伊朗正在研发的核武器计划

sentences.en: is a much more existential threat to Israel than anything Hamas or other Palestinians might throw at the Israeli population.
sentences.zh: 对以色列构成的生存威胁远大于哈马斯或其他巴勒斯坦人可能对以色列民众造成的任何威胁。

sentences.en: And therefore, by this argument, some Israeli leaders, perhaps Netanyahu himself, is searching for a pretext to hit Iran hard, to destroy that nuclear capacity,
sentences.zh: 因此，根据这一论点，一些以色列领导人，也许是内塔尼亚胡本人，正在寻找一个借口来重创伊朗，摧毁其核能力，

sentences.en: and perhaps even drag in the US, Israel's biggest ally, into a regional war that it doesn't seek, but would be forced to join in order to defend its key Middle Eastern ally.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能将以色列最大的盟友美国拖入一场它并不寻求但为了保卫其关键中东盟友而被迫加入的地区战争。

sentences.en: And all of that would create the pretext and the opportunity to destroy Iran's nuclear capability.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都将创造摧毁伊朗核能力的借口和机会。

sentences.en: So, as much as many Israelis and Palestinians are desperately looking for a way to end this war, there are people on either side who have reasons to not just continue the war,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管许多以色列人和巴勒斯坦人都在拼命寻找结束这场战争的方法，但双方都有人有理由不仅继续战争，

sentences.en: but also escalate it into an all-out regional conflict.
sentences.zh: 而且将其升级为全面的地区冲突。

sentences.en: I mean, it's remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很了不起。

sentences.en: You know, we started this conversation by talking about these two men, their political ambitions, and why it's making it difficult for them to get to a ceasefire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们开始这次谈话时谈到了这两个人，他们的政治抱负，以及为什么这使得他们难以达成停火。

sentences.en: But we're ending it in a place where it seems not only are they not wanting to get to a ceasefire, but potentially they actually want the war to get bigger.
sentences.zh: 但我们结束时却发现，似乎他们不仅不想达成停火，而且可能实际上希望战争规模扩大。

sentences.en: They're not going away from conflict, but running toward it.
sentences.zh: 他们不是在远离冲突，而是在奔向冲突。

sentences.en: That's a possibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可能性。

sentences.en: We can't know what either man is thinking exactly.
sentences.zh: 我们无法确切知道这两个人在想什么。

sentences.en: We're not inside their heads.
sentences.zh: 我们不是他们肚子里的蛔虫。

sentences.en: What we can say for sure, though, is that both Israel and Hamas, and by extension, both Netanyahu and Sinoah, are still involved in negotiations for a ceasefire.
sentences.zh: 不过我们可以肯定地说，以色列和哈马斯，进而内塔尼亚胡和辛瓦尔，都仍在参与停火谈判。

sentences.en: Those negotiations do not currently seem very likely to succeed, but they do continue.
sentences.zh: 这些谈判目前看起来不太可能成功，但它们确实在继续。

sentences.en: There was a big meeting on Sunday between senior officials from Israel and the mediating countries.
sentences.zh: 周日，以色列高级官员与调解国之间举行了一次重要会议。

sentences.en: The possibility of a ceasefire very much remains, even if the chances of an all-out regional war are also growing.
sentences.zh: 停火的可能性依然很大，即使全面地区战争的可能性也在增加。

sentences.en: Patrick, thank you.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, hundreds of Israeli troops mounted a major military operation in the West Bank, targeting Palestinian militants in the occupied territory,
sentences.zh: 周三，数百名以色列军队在约旦河西岸发动了一次重大军事行动，针对被占领土上的巴勒斯坦武装分子，

sentences.en: where nearly three million Palestinians live under Israeli military rule.
sentences.zh: 那里有近三百万巴勒斯坦人在以色列军事统治下生活。

sentences.en: The operation followed months of escalating Israeli raids in the area, and Israeli officials said that at least nine people had been killed.
sentences.zh: 此次行动是在该地区以色列突袭行动升级数月后进行的，以色列官员称至少有九人死亡。

sentences.en: Hamas denounced the operation, accusing Israel of expanding the war in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯谴责了这次行动，指责以色列扩大了加沙战争。

sentences.en: As of Wednesday morning, the operation was ongoing.
sentences.zh: 截至周三上午，行动仍在进行中。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Donald Trump announced plans to name his former rival, Robert F.
sentences.zh: 周二，唐纳德·特朗普宣布计划任命他曾经的竞争对手小罗伯特·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy Jr., along with former U.S.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪，以及前美国

sentences.en: Representative Tulsi Gabbard, as honorary co-chairs of his presidential transition team.
sentences.zh: 众议员图尔西·加巴德，担任他总统过渡团队的名誉联席主席。

sentences.en: The team, which includes Trump's sons, as well as his running mate, J.D.
sentences.zh: 该团队包括特朗普的儿子们，以及他的竞选搭档J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, would help him select the policies and personnel for a second Trump term.
sentences.zh: 万斯，将帮助他为第二个特朗普任期挑选政策和人员。

sentences.en: The appointments were a bid by Trump to show that his support extends beyond party lines.
sentences.zh: 这些任命是特朗普试图表明他的支持超越了党派界限。

sentences.en: Both Kennedy and Gabbard spent most of their public lives as progressives, and both started their presidential runs as Democrats.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪和加巴德的大部分公众生活都是进步派，两人最初都是以民主党人的身份开始竞选总统的。

sentences.en: Kennedy ended his independent campaign for president last week and endorsed Trump.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪上周结束了他的独立总统竞选并支持特朗普。

sentences.en: Gabbard has since left the Democratic Party and rebranded herself as a celebrity among Trump's base of support.
sentences.zh: 加巴德此后离开了民主党，并将自己重塑为特朗普支持者中的名人。

sentences.en: And Special Counsel Jack Smith revised his indictment accusing former President Donald Trump
sentences.zh: 特别检察官杰克·史密斯修改了他的起诉书，指控前总统唐纳德·特朗普

sentences.en: of plotting to overturn the 2020 election in an effort to help it survive the Supreme Court's recent ruling, granting former presidents immunity for official acts in office.
sentences.zh: 密谋推翻2020年选举，以帮助其在最高法院最近裁定前总统享有官方行为豁免权的判决下幸存。

sentences.en: In its decision on immunity, the Supreme Court ruled that a president's dealings with the Justice Department are considered official duties of his office.
sentences.zh: 在关于豁免权的裁决中，最高法院裁定总统与司法部的往来被视为其职位的官方职责。

sentences.en: Smith's revised charging documents exclude the accusations that Trump conspired with Justice Department officials
sentences.zh: 史密斯修改后的指控文件排除了特朗普与司法部官员串通的指控，

sentences.en: to support his false claims that the election had been stolen from him.
sentences.zh: 以支持他关于选举被窃取的虚假主张。
